title: Dense network layer for the geo map
summary: A country-sized network (hundreds of thousands of nodes and segments) drawn as one base layer of a GeoMap: built once from typed arrays into a few GeoJSON features per category, width by weight bucket, categories toggled by visibility, dimmed under overlays, nodes and segments picked through grid indexes instead of per-feature hits; plus GeoPathFlow, comets travelling along every overlay path, and PlaceLabels, the basemap's place names restyled from the theme and lifted above the network so they stay readable.
useWhen: the base network is too big for GeoSurface (more than ~10k nodes or segments): a national transport, road, grid or telecom network
segments fall into categories to toggle (mode, voltage, operator) and carry a weight (routes, capacity)
a route should visibly travel along the map (GeoPathFlow)
avoidWhen: a few thousand nodes: GeoSurface draws and labels them itself

provenance.what: built for the UK public transport map (389k stops, 417k segments)

verified: unit tests (buckets, collections, node and segment grids, polyline interpolation); uktransport: 389,239 stops and 416,604 grouped segments drawn, stops and segments picked on OpenFreeMap dark
